column2: Sinai wilderness, tent, first day, second month and second year locate the census. The time is measured from the exodus.
Take the sum renders the census idiom. Family, ancestral house, name and individual head are all retained; every male continues into the age condition.
Twenty and upward and military service define the group. Both Moses and Aaron perform registration; the repeated instruction remains.
One ruler per tribe accompanies them, with ancestral-house affiliation. The compact Greek grouping remains provisionally represented.
column3: How should the repeated distributive hekastos and rulers genitive be construed most naturally?

column2: Reuben's representative is Elizur son of Shedeur. The Greek name forms are recorded separately; inherited English forms are retained pending authority approval.
Simeon's representative is Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai, corresponding to Salamiel and Sourisadai in the source. No identity change is inferred from spelling.
Judah's representative is Nahshon son of Amminadab. The pairing and tribe agree with the named Greek entry.
Issachar's representative is Nethanel son of Zuar. The source's Sogar form is recorded as an alias question, not silently treated as a different father.
Zebulun's representative is Eliab son of Helon. The Chailon source form remains in the working name record.
Joseph's sons are represented through Ephraim and Manasseh, with separate leader/father pairs. Both subgroups remain in this single stored unit.
Benjamin's representative is Abidan son of Gideoni. The inherited form maps to Gadeoni without a new editorial name approval.
Dan's representative is Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai. The tribe and both personal identities remain distinct from the similarly ending earlier name.
Asher's representative is Pagiel son of Ocran. Phagaiel and Echran are the selected source forms, retained in the working register.
Gad's representative is Eliasaph son of Reuel. The Greek Ragouel is preserved as evidence; no Deuel harmonization is made.
Naphtali's representative is Ahira son of Enan. Achire and Ainan are recorded as source forms without guessing a new identity.
Called representatives are tribal rulers and commanders of thousands. The military term is not flattened into generic elders.
Moses and Aaron take the men called by name. The named selection links directly to the preceding list.
The first day, month and second-year wording is unusual beside verse 1. The inherited date remains provisional; descent and name-based male registration are retained.
column3: Does tou deuterou qualify month or year in the transmitted phrase, and how should the extra etous be understood?

column2: The command to Moses governs registration in Sinai. The passive registration does not invent additional census agents.
Reuben is explicitly Israel's firstborn. Family, division, ancestral house, names, heads, male sex, age and military eligibility all remain in the formula.
Reuben's figure is 46,500; the Greek thousands and hundreds match the written English number.
Simeon's census repeats the full descent, name, head, age and army criteria. The repeated administrative detail is not abbreviated away.
Simeon's figure is 59,300; both components agree with the Greek number words.
Judah's formula includes divisions as well as families and ancestral houses. Every male and the age/military conditions remain.
Judah's enrolment is 74,600, preserving the Greek tens-of-thousands and hundreds values.
Issachar's formula retains the same named and individual census categories rather than reporting only a tribal total.
Issachar's enrolment is 54,400, with no rounding or normalization.
Zebulun's census retains family, division and house distinctions plus age and military eligibility.
Zebulun's enrolment is 57,400, matching the selected Greek figure.
Ephraim is explicitly introduced as sons of Joseph, followed by the full formula. That additional genealogy is retained.
Ephraim's total is 40,500, including the five-hundred remainder.
Manasseh has its own complete formula after Ephraim. The common Joseph connection is not repeated where absent.
Manasseh's total is 32,200, distinct from Ephraim's figure.
Benjamin's census preserves every male, twenty and upward, and army participation, alongside the descent categories.
Benjamin's enrolment is 35,400, agreeing with the source numeral sequence.
Gad follows Benjamin in this census list, though appearing earlier in the leader list. The source order is preserved.
Gad's total is 45,650; the extra fifty is explicit and must not be lost among the rounded hundreds elsewhere.
Dan's entry repeats the full registration criteria. No stylistic compression replaces the source repetition.
Dan's enrolment is 62,700, preserving both number components.
Asher's entry includes the divisions category and the same age and military criteria as the preceding tribes.
Asher's enrolment is 41,500; the one-thousand component is retained.
Naphtali closes the tribal formulas with the same name/head and age/army qualifications.
Naphtali's enrolment is 53,400, matching the Greek total.
Moses, Aaron and twelve tribal rulers perform the census. The twelve refers to the representatives, not a combined headcount including Moses and Aaron.
The overall enrolment again specifies twenty and upward and going out to battle. The military scope remains explicit.
The total is 603,550. The twelve individually read tribal totals independently sum to this number; no numerical correction is needed.
Levites are excluded from this Israelite military registration. The exception does not assert that they are outside Israel altogether.
The Lord's speech introduces the explanation of the Levitical exception.
Do not register together and do not include their number are both stated. The emphatic see instruction remains.
Levites oversee, carry, minister in and camp around the tent and all furnishings. Their repeated explicit agency is retained.
They dismantle at departure and erect at encampment. Outsider concerns unauthorized approach to this service context, not automatically a foreign national.
Each Israelite camps by formation and command with the army. Both organizational terms remain distinct.
Levitical encampment is before the Lord and prevents offence in this Greek reading. Wrath is not substituted for hamartema.
The Greek names both Moses and Aaron as command recipients. The repeated they did closes the account.
The divine speech explicitly addresses Moses and Aaron together, continuing the camp organization.
Each camps beside another by formation, signs and ancestral houses, opposite and around the tent. No distance measurement is inserted.
Judah's camp is first and eastward, led by Nahshon son of Amminadab. Both directional and sequence information remain.
Judah's army remains 74,600, matching its chapter 1 census.
Issachar camps adjacent, with Nethanel son of Zuar. The leader/father pairing matches the earlier list.
Issachar's army remains 54,400, without an inferred change between censuses.
Zebulun camps next, with Eliab son of Helon. The adjacency phrase does not add a new compass direction.
Zebulun's army remains 57,400. The count agrees with chapter 1.
The eastern group totals 186,400 and departs first. Its three tribal totals sum to the stated group figure.
Reuben's direction is lips, inherited southwest, not automatically harmonized to south. Elizur and Shedeur remain the leader pair.
column3: Does the directional term indicate southwest strictly or a broader southern quarter here?

column2: Reuben's army remains 46,500, corresponding to its earlier registration.
Simeon camps beside Reuben, led by Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai. Adjacency and kinship remain clear.
Simeon's army remains 59,300. No additional troop category is implied by the formula.
Gad completes this group under Eliasaph son of Reuel. The selected Ragouel reading remains consistent.
Gad's army is 45,650, retaining the distinctive fifty remainder.
Reuben's group totals 151,450 and departs second. The sum of Reuben, Simeon and Gad agrees.

Propose shall set out for shall be raised: the tent and Levitical camp move among the marching camps, and the following clause explicitly compares camping with departure. The close draft retains shall be taken up.
Ephraim's group is toward the sea, retaining the source's geographic expression. Elishama son of Ammihud leads it.
Ephraim's army remains 40,500, consistent with the first census.
Manasseh camps adjacent with Gamaliel son of Pedahzur. Both identities are preserved.
Manasseh's army remains 32,200, as previously registered.
Benjamin camps next with Abidan son of Gideoni. The source does not repeat Joseph's parentage here.
Benjamin's army is 35,400, unchanged from chapter 1.
Ephraim's group totals 108,100 and leaves third. The three constituent numbers sum to this figure.
Dan's group is northward, with Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai. Direction and leader are both explicit.
Dan's army remains 62,700, matching the census figure.
Asher camps beside Dan under Pagiel son of Ocran. The adjacency relation is retained.
Asher's army remains 41,500. The number agrees with the earlier list.
Naphtali is adjacent under Ahira son of Enan. No new name normalization is introduced.
Naphtali's army remains 53,400, completing the northern group's components.
Dan's group totals 157,600 and departs last by formation. Last is the selected ordinal description, not a supplied fourth.
The four groups total 603,550, matching chapter 1. Ancestral houses and armies remain part of the census description.
Levites again remain outside the combined registration, according to the command to Moses.
Both camping and departure obey the command. Formation, adjacency, division and ancestral house all remain in the closing summary.
